page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6r.2xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server powered by an 8-core Ampere Altra ARM64 processor operating at 2.8 GHz. It is provisioned with 8 dedicated vCPUs and 16.0 GB of system memory, providing a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The instance carries no local NVMe storage and includes no integrated GPU hardware. Network connectivity is delivered via a baseline bandwidth capacity of 2 Gbps.

Performance metrics indicate strong multi-threaded scaling alongside moderate single-threaded processing capabilities. In execution testing, the server achieves average scores across multi-core benchmarks, such as 14,295.27 in stress-ng multi-core and 6,139.0 in Geekbench multi-core. Software compilation workloads yield a Geekbench Clang score of 9,709.0, while Redis SET performance reaches 11.05 million operations per second. Conversely, single-threaded throughput reflects weaker performance tiers, highlighted by a single-core Geekbench score of 1,104.0, single-threaded gzip compression at 23.76 GB/sec, and a weak PassMark memory score of 1,635.78.

The ARM-based architecture provides efficient core-scaling density for scale-out cloud environments, though it lacks x86 extended instruction sets such as AVX and AMX. The absence of local disk drives requires reliance on attached block storage for persistent data requirements. Overall, the resource profile is best aligned with multi-threaded web serving, containerized microservices, software build pipelines, key-value caching, and general ARM-native utility processing.

It includes no local storage or GPU accelerators. In performance testing, the instance demonstrates moderate multi-threaded efficiency, reaching 14,295.27 in stress-ng multi-core, 11.05 million Redis SET operations per second, and a Clang compilation score of 9,709.0. However, single-core processing metrics remain in lower benchmark brackets, reflected by a Geekbench single-core score of 1,104.0 and reduced single-threaded compression speeds. Without local disk storage, persistent volumes must be attached remotely. The instance offers resource density for multi-threaded cloud workloads, such as software compilation, static web serving, caching, and ARM-native microservices.
